_comment: Where build_videos.py looks for each app channel's highlights.
'playlist' is preferred over an uploads feed wherever the series curates a
season-highlights playlist: it is their own selection, so no title has to be
pattern-matched and nothing unrelated slips in. Where there is no playlist,
the uploads feed is narrowed by 'titleMatch' (case-insensitive).
'enabled: false' entries are audited and deliberately parked, not untried —
the 'note' says what is wrong. Turning one on is a one-line edit here plus a
promotion to live; it needs no app release.
Embeddability is a per-CHANNEL setting that no API field exposes: the Data API's
status.embeddable is true for videos the Formula 1 channel then refuses to play
with error 150. The only test is playing one. Before enabling a source here,
play one of its videos in the app and confirm no error appears.
A 'feeds' list draws one app channel from several YouTube channels, merged newest-first.
'label' is the heading the apps show (default 'Highlights'); 'credit' is the line under it.
Region data comes in two shapes and they are NOT equivalent: 'blocked' is a short exclusion
list, 'allowed' is a whitelist that hides the video from everywhere else. Sky Sports F1 allows
six countries. Anything with an allow-list is invisible to most of the world, so weigh that

sources.label: F1 Video
sources.credit: the F1 teams and the FIA
sources.note: Formula 1's own channel refuses to be embedded — error 150 on every video tried, including its F2 and F3 reels, and the Data API reports all of them as embeddable, so it is only visible by playing one. There is therefore no way to show F1 race highlights at all. These four official channels are the honest substitute: all verified embeddable and, unlike Sky, unrestricted worldwide. The section is labelled 'F1 Video' rather than 'Highlights' because that is what it is. A 5-minute floor (minSeconds) keeps the section to features, onboards and podcasts; without it the teams' social clips — paddock cooking, birthday messages — dominate it.
BLOCKED: published on the Formula 1 channel, which refuses embedding (error 150). See the f1 note. F2 has no channel of its own — @Formula2 is a squatter and the real one stopped in 2023.
BLOCKED: published on the Formula 1 channel, which refuses embedding (error 150). See the f1 note.
Verified embeddable in the simulator. The best-served channel of the thirteen: a ~15 min race edit, a ~57 min extended cut and a final-laps clip after every round.
Verified embeddable in the simulator. Posts per-stage highlights through a rally as well as an event round-up, so this channel fills faster than the others.
Verified embeddable in the simulator. ~30 min Cup highlights, and unusually the full replays play outside the US too.
Verified embeddable in the simulator. Deliberately excludes 'Full Race' uploads: those are geo-blocked outside the US, while the highlight edits are not.
Verified embeddable, but the season ended August 2026 so the feed is compilations rather than race edits. Turn on when the Gen4 season opens.

Active, but the naming is inconsistent and the feed is mostly support series and shorts. The titleMatch here is a guess and needs a season watched before it is trusted. Note @imsaracing is a dead duplicate.
Verified embeddable. Highlights are branded 'ON THE LIMIT: Round N' with no 'highlights' in the title — hence the anchored pattern. Low volume, 1-20k views.
Verified embeddable, but full 42-minute races only, no highlight edits, and the feed is shared with Clio Trophy rallying. Enabling this would put hour-long uploads under a 'Highlights' heading.

No compliant source. The official channel is clips and shorts only; the 'Full Race and Sprint Highlights' playlist that looks official belongs to TNT Sports, a UK broadcaster, and everything else is behind paid VideoPass. Leave off until MotoGP itself posts race edits.
